samples.summary: A task checkbox inside a `<details>` foldout is unclickable AND its DOM state is left desynced from the note
samples.evidence: `onTaskClick` bails at `if (target.closest('a, button, details')) return;` (preview.ts:278) BEFORE the `if (onCheckbox) e.preventDefault();` at line 288. `details-plugin.ts` parses the foldout body as ordinary markdown, so a task list inside `<details>` renders real, enabled checkboxes (the preview root carries `note-tasks-interactive`, so they also show a pointer cursor). Clicking such a checkbox: (a) never calls `onToggleTask`, so the source is never written — the task is simply not togglable inside a foldout; and worse (b) the browser has already flipped `input.checked` and the click is *not* cancelled, and since no document changed there is no `docChanged` re-render to restore it — the preview now displays a ticked box for a task the note still records as unticked, indefinitely. This is exactly the failure mode the comment at lines 283-287 says it is guarding against; the `details` exemption is placed on the wrong side of the `preventDefault`. The new tests only cover the inverse nesting (a `<details>` inside a task item), so nothing catches it.

samples.summary: toggleOrderedList renumbers per indent level but does not widen child indents, so nested lists are flattened / renumbered wrongly
samples.evidence:
`toggleKind` writes `${n}.` while leaving `p.indent` untouched (list-commands.ts:241-244). An ordered marker is 2+ columns wide where a bullet is 1, so converting `- a
  - b` (or the test's `a
  b`) yields `1. a
  1. b`: the child sits at column 2 but the parent item's content column is now 3. CommonMark/markdown-it therefore no longer treats `  1. b` as nested content — it becomes a *sibling* of `1. a` (indent < 4 and marker matches), so the preview renders `1. a / 2. b`, contradicting both the source text and the per-level counters the function just computed. The nesting the user had is silently lost on a single toolbar click. `indentList` gets this right (it uses `contentColumn`, i.e. 3 for `1. `), which shows the intended invariant; `toggleKind` violates it. list-commands.test.ts:88-97 asserts only the raw string `'1. a
  1. b
  2. c
2. d'`, so it passes while the rendered result is wrong.

samples.summary: The bare-`[ ]` input rule fires inside fenced/indented code blocks, corrupting code content
samples.evidence: `noteCheckboxInput` only checks the typed char, `state.readOnly` and `EditorView.editable`; it never consults the markdown syntax tree (`@codemirror/language` `syntaxTree`, available since `markdown()` is loaded at editor.ts:408). So typing a space after a line-leading `[ ]`/`[x]` inside a ``` fence, or in a 4-space-indented code block, rewrites the user's code line to `- [ ] ` — a silent content mutation that is synced to peers. Documenting checkbox markdown inside a fence (which this repo's own docs do) hits it.

samples.summary: Task items inside a blockquote get clickable checkboxes whose click silently does nothing
samples.evidence: `LIST_RE` (`^(\s*)([-*+]|\d{1,9}[.)])...`) only allows whitespace before the marker, so a line `> - [ ] x` parses with `marker: ''` and `check: null`; `setTaskChecked` (line 302) returns early. But the preview still renders that item with an enabled checkbox and tags it with `data-source-line`, and `onTaskClick` cancels the click (preview.ts:288) — so the user clicks a pointer-cursor checkbox inside a quote and absolutely nothing happens, with no feedback. The same applies to `toggleBulletList`/`toggleTaskList`/`indentList` on quoted lines: `prefixOf` for a non-marker line returns only the indent, so toggling a bullet on `> text` produces `- > text`, changing the block's meaning.

samples.summary: The `e.detail > 1` guard does not actually prevent a double-click text selection from editing the note
samples.evidence: A double-click delivers click #1 with `detail === 1` and click #2 with `detail === 2`. The guard at line 295 only drops #2, so click #1 has already run the full path and toggled the source line (and, via `docChanged`, re-rendered the preview and synced the edit to peers). The stated intent — "Selecting a task's text must not rewrite it" — is therefore not achieved for the common word-select gesture; only the redundant second toggle is suppressed. `selectionTouches` cannot help either, because on click #1 the selection is still collapsed.

samples.summary: Multi-cursor: the input handler consumes the typed space for all ranges but only edits the main one
samples.evidence: The handler dispatches `changes: { from: line.from, to, insert }` for the main range and returns `true` (checkbox-input.ts:36-44). Returning `true` tells CodeMirror the input was fully handled, so with multiple selection ranges every non-main cursor loses the typed space entirely instead of inserting it. The same single-range assumption runs through `list-commands.ts` (`selectedLines` reads `state.selection.main` only), so a list toggle with multiple cursors silently applies to just one of them.

samples.summary: indent/outdent skips plain lines inside the selection, breaking the block's relative shape
samples.evidence: `shift` returns `prefixOf(p)` unchanged for any target line without a marker (line 270), while every list line moves by `step`. A selection mixing an item with its plain continuation/paragraph lines therefore shifts the markers but leaves the prose behind, which changes how markdown reads the continuation (it can drop out of the item, or become a 4-space code block). The doc comment on `indentStep` claims "nesting relationships inside the selection are preserved", which only holds for all-list selections.

finding.summary: A task checkbox inside a `<details>` foldout is unclickable AND its DOM state is left desynced from the note
finding.evidence: `onTaskClick` bails at `if (target.closest('a, button, details')) return;` (preview.ts:278) BEFORE the `if (onCheckbox) e.preventDefault();` at line 288. `details-plugin.ts` parses the foldout body as ordinary markdown, so a task list inside `<details>` renders real, enabled checkboxes (the preview root carries `note-tasks-interactive`, so they also show a pointer cursor). Clicking such a checkbox: (a) never calls `onToggleTask`, so the source is never written — the task is simply not togglable inside a foldout; and worse (b) the browser has already flipped `input.checked` and the click is *not* cancelled, and since no document changed there is no `docChanged` re-render to restore it — the preview now displays a ticked box for a task the note still records as unticked, indefinitely. This is exactly the failure mode the comment at lines 283-287 says it is guarding against; the `details` exemption is placed on the wrong side of the `preventDefault`. The new tests only cover the inverse nesting (a `<details>` inside a task item), so nothing catches it.

verdict.reason: The described code is present verbatim: preview.ts:278 returns on `target.closest('a, button, details')` before the compensating `if (onCheckbox) e.preventDefault()` at preview.ts:288, whose own comment (lines 283-287) states the cancel must precede any bailing guard precisely to avoid leaving the preview showing state the note does not have. details-plugin.ts (doc lines 22-34, rule 46-96) parses the foldout body as ordinary markdown, and preview.ts:53 enables task-list checkboxes while preview.ts:335-338 only disables them for read-only previews, so a `- [ ]` inside `<details>` renders a live, enabled checkbox (cursor:pointer via notes-preview.css:344-346). Clicking it bails at line 278: onToggleTask never fires (task untogglable inside a foldout) and the click is not cancelled, so the browser-flipped `checked` persists with no docChanged re-render (per the comment at preview.ts:262-266) to correct it. The existing test at preview.test.ts:192-220 only covers the inverse nesting (a details inside a task item), so nothing catches this. No guard, CSS, or other handler makes the path unreachable. Real logic bug with persistent UI/source desync — blocking under the correctness rubric (major/critical impact: broken core flow plus desynced state).

finding.evidence:
`toggleKind` writes `${n}.` while leaving `p.indent` untouched (list-commands.ts:241-244). An ordered marker is 2+ columns wide where a bullet is 1, so converting `- a
  - b` (or the test's `a
  b`) yields `1. a
  1. b`: the child sits at column 2 but the parent item's content column is now 3. CommonMark/markdown-it therefore no longer treats `  1. b` as nested content — it becomes a *sibling* of `1. a` (indent < 4 and marker matches), so the preview renders `1. a / 2. b`, contradicting both the source text and the per-level counters the function just computed.   1. b
  2. c
2. d'`, so it passes while the rendered result is wrong.

verdict.reason:
The ordered branch of toggleKind (list-commands.ts:241-244) rewrites the marker to `${n}.` while copying p.indent verbatim, so a child item's indent is not widened to the parent's new content column. The file itself encodes the opposite invariant: contentColumn (64-66) and indentStep (155-165) deliberately use 3 columns for `1. `, and the test at list-commands.test.ts:179-185 asserts `'1. a
   2. b'` ("Three columns, not two"). Converting `- a
  - b` (or the fixture `a
  b`) therefore yields `1. a
  1. b`, where the child's indent (2) is below the parent's content column (3); under CommonMark/markdown-it the child stops being nested content and becomes a sibling of the same ordered list, so the preview renders 1./2./3./4. and contradicts the per-level counters the function just computed. The path is real and unguarded: notes-toolbar.tsx:303-310 -> editor.ts:581-582 -> list-commands.ts:255-261, with the preview rendered by markdown-it (packages/notes/package.json:65) whose only overridden block rules are the empty-bullet and lheading rules (list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:56-174), none of which relax list indentation. The existing test asserts only the raw string (list-commands.test.ts:68-77), so it passes while nesting is silently flattened. Real logic bug / broken invariant with user-visible structure loss on one click: blocking under the correctness rubric at major severity.
